intended_object: Given a locally constant function f : Spec R → ℕ, take the canonical finite projective module realizing f as its rank. This abbreviation gives the constant rank on a nonempty fiber j of that module's rank function, which is the value of f on that fiber. Inferred from the docstring and the surrounding CanonicalRealization section.
explanation:
The body is `rankFiberRank R (ofLocallyConstantRank R f) j`. Here `rankFiberRank` is `Function.Fiber.image (rankLocallyConstant R M) i`, the common value of the stalk-rank function on the fiber i. So the abbreviation gives the rank of the canonical realization of f on one of its nonempty rank fibers. That rank equals the value of f on the fiber, as the lemma `locallyConstantRankFiberRank_le_rankBound` uses via `rankAtStalk_ofLocallyConstantRank`.

It is correct for what it says. But it is a bookkeeping device: it specializes a general construction to the library's own canonical realization `ofLocallyConstantRank`, and it is indexed by `locallyConstantRankFiberIndex`, another internal abbreviation. Its only job is to support the proofs about threshold idempotents and the componentwise-free model in this file (e.g. `rankIdempotent_mul_locallyConstantRankFiberIdempotent`). The literature has no separate notion matching it; mathematically it is just "the value of f on the fiber". So there is no faithfulness or generality question to settle, and it is classified as a technical device.
